commands.name: api-login
commands.description: Sign in with an API key or an email address and password, and save the sign-in (checked with the API first)

arguments.name: auth-type
arguments.description: key (an API key) or user (an email address and password)

arguments.name: identifier
arguments.description: For key: the API key as <userId>:<secret>, or the user id alone; for user: the email address

arguments.name: credential
arguments.description: The key's secret or the password; leave it out to type it unseen, or pipe it on standard input

options.name: no-verify
options.description: Save without checking the sign-in with the API first

commands.notes:
Forms:
  api-login key <userId>:<secret>     the API key as one value (what MAITENTO_API_KEY holds)
  api-login key <userId> [secret]     leave the secret out to type it unseen, or pipe it: echo "$SECRET" | mt api-login key <userId>
  api-login user <email> [password]   an email address and password; leave the password out to type it unseen
The user id is the id of the USER who owns the key, not the key's own id: api-key-create and the portal show it with the secret.
The sign-in is checked with the API (GET /users/self) before it is saved; one the API rejects is not saved.
Saved sign-ins: on Windows, encrypted with DPAPI for your account; on macOS/Linux, NOT encrypted, in ~/.maitento/settings.json,
which only your user can read (mode 600). Where that matters, prefer MAITENTO_API_KEY from your own secret store.

Environment (overrides the saved settings for this process only; never saved):
  MAITENTO_API_KEY     an API key, <userId>:<secret>, used instead of the saved login
  MAITENTO_BASE_URL    the API URL, instead of the one api-url-set saved
  MAITENTO_NAMESPACE   the default namespace, instead of the one ns-set saved
  MAITENTO_CONFIG_DIR  the folder settings.json is kept in (default ~/.maitento)
Precedence: a command's own --namespace, then these variables, then the saved settings. 'config-get' shows what is in effect.
